market_holds: Spot about $47.2 intraday (Yahoo chart, 19:19 UTC 2026-11-24), down about 15% today. Today was a broad chip selloff: SOXX fell about 7% intraday and the SOX closed about 6% lower per the search summaries. AMBA is -23% since 2026-10-14 against SOXX -25%, so most of the 20-day -27% (baseline) is sector beta and not a stock-specific repricing. It sits at its 52-week low, 48% below the high. Options (baseline, 18:08 UTC): an event-implied move of 12.7%, ATM IV 166%, skew -6.9 vol points (calls dearer than puts), put/call OI 0.23, an ATM spread of 52% of mid, so the price is indicative only. Usual reaction: a median absolute move of 16.8%, down after 6 of the last 7 prints, including -21% after an in-line guide in May 2026; the one mild reaction (-0.8%, Sep 2026) came with a guide above consensus. Consensus (Yahoo analysis page, read 2026-11-24): Q3 (Oct) $119.8M against the company's $115-124M guide; Q4 (Jan) $112.6M (range $109.4-116.8M, 11 analysts), which is -6% q/q and the same as the -7% of a normal year. FY27 is $441M (+12.9%). Q4 EPS is $0.19, down from $0.21 90 days ago, with 8 cuts and 2 raises over 30 days. Short interest is 4.65M shares on 2026-10-30, about 2.6 days to cover, falling from 5.7M in mid-September (Nasdaq). Management said on the Sep 3 call that Q4 should follow regular seasonality 'barring any memory impact' and called Q4 the uncertainty.
view: This print trades on the Q4 (January) guide and what management says about memory. Q3 should land inside or above its guide, since Ambarella has beaten revenue for several quarters and the Q3 guide was a big raise. Q4 consensus of $112.6M still assumes the normal seasonal dip with no memory hit, so it still holds the call's 'barring memory' case. Since that call, the memory squeeze got clearly worse. GoPro's 10-Q reports memory price jumps of 70-80% in the last week of September. Qualcomm (Nov 6) says handset makers buy chips only to match the memory they can get. Synaptics (Nov 5) missed revenue by about 7% on memory constraints. Arlo flags memory costs for Q4. Hikvision built inventory ahead of cost rises, which could have pulled orders into Ambarella's Q3 and left Q4 thinner. All of that points to a Q4 guide midpoint under $112.6M, which I put at about 60-65%. Against it: Ambarella's auto business is at a record, its enterprise security customers are less price-sensitive, management says it is helping customers find workarounds and that its parts need little DRAM, and Hikvision's Q3 revenue still grew 13.7%. On price, the stock has already fallen 15% today and sits at its low, with calls bid over puts, so a soft guide partly meets low expectations and an in-line guide could bring a sharp relief rally. Weighing a likely soft guide against a washed-out tape and the name's habit of falling on prints, I lean slightly down, but not far enough to bet. The overnight window also carries heavy sector beta after a 6% SOX day, which adds noise in both directions.
unpriced: Possibly the memory effect on the Q4 guide. Consensus for the January quarter ($112.6M) still matches normal seasonality, although management made that conditional on memory and the memory shortage worsened after the call. Revenue estimates were not revised for it, only EPS was trimmed slightly. But the stock's 15% fall today and 23% fall over the month may already price a soft guide, even though most of the month's fall tracks the sector. I cannot show which side of that the price sits on, so the edge is weak.

recommendation.reason: A Q4 guide below the seasonal $112.6M consensus is more likely than not, given memory evidence dated after the last call (GoPro, Qualcomm, Synaptics). But the stock has already collapsed into the print (-15% today, at its 52-week low, calls bid), and the overnight window carries heavy sector beta. My directional probability is well under the 65 needed to recommend.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide midpoint at or above about $112M, with management saying memory has not hurt customer orders, would make a relief rally from this washed-out level the likely outcome.

self_critique: The memory evidence comes from smartphone and consumer peers. Ambarella's mix (auto at a record, enterprise security, a small DRAM footprint) may be much less exposed, and Hikvision's growth suggests security-camera demand held. The stock has already fallen 15% today into the print, calls cost more than puts, and short interest is falling, so even a modest guide cut could be met with relief from a capitulation low. The overnight sector move after a 6% SOX day could swamp anything company-specific. That is why I stay close to 50.
approach_notes: The P4 point that a fact in the news is not the same as being priced helped: checking the actual Q4 consensus against management's conditional seasonality gave the one concrete gap. P6's 'find the line' pointed straight at the Q4 guide. The playbook has no guidance on separating sector beta from a pre-print fall on a violent sector day, which was the main ambiguity here.
